basis: Glycosylation defect with CNS disease and deafness; arthrogryposis 80-99%. Cap omits visual impairment (30-79%; reduced acuity 3/3) and coagulopathy (30-79%).

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment qualifies (30-79%; reduced acuity 3/3), but the cap favors arthrogryposis (80-99%).
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: arthrogryposis affects 80-99%, causing fixed joint and limb abnormalities; prioritized under the cap.

basis: Tongue hypoplasia and limb reduction define the syndrome. Nail morphology abnormalities (30-79%) lack evidence of functional damage; intellectual disability is below 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: abnormal fingernail morphology occurs in 30-79%, but this nonspecific finding does not establish direct skin or nail damage or loss of function.

basis: CoQ10 biosynthesis disorder; encephalopathy, developmental delay, seizures and ataxia affect 3/3. Eye movement abnormalities are neurologic; muscle fiber predominance alone is not muscle damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy, developmental delay, seizures and ataxia occur in 3/3, documenting CNS damage from the metabolic defect.

basis: Progressive cerebellar and motor-neuron disease. Muscle wasting (30-79%) is neurogenic; ocular pursuit abnormalities reflect CNS dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy (30-79%) reflects denervation from motor-neuron disease, without evidence of direct muscle pathology; skeletal deformities occur in under 30%.

basis: Diabetes and optic atrophy define the syndrome (16/16). Deafness affects 14/16 (~88%); characteristic peptic ulceration 11/16 (~69%). Platelet dysfunction omitted under the cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects 14/16 (~88%); diabetes and optic atrophy are the defining diagnostic pair.

basis: Lymphoblast malignancy of blood and marrow; direct hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 50-70%. CNS involvement is a minority.

decisions.hepatic: involved: leukemic liver infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 50-70% of children, representing direct organ occupation.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: this concept is leukemia of blood and marrow; lymphoid lineage and shared lymphoma ancestry alone do not establish lymphoma or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Lymphoplasmacytic B-cell neoplasia; alpha HCD accounts for most cases (~60-75%) and usually infiltrates small intestine, supporting gastrointestinal involvement in over 30% overall.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: alpha HCD predominates (~60-75% of cases) and usually causes intestinal infiltration with malabsorption; this exceeds 30% across the umbrella.

basis: Neonatal diabetes, epiphyseal dysplasia and recurrent liver failure define WRS; neutropenia occurs in 30-79%. Renal and neurologic findings occur in under 30%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: recurrent acute liver failure is explicitly part of the disease definition; liver abnormalities affect 80-99% and acute hepatic failure 30-79%.

basis: BBS4-associated Bardet-Biedl phenotype includes retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly. Renal disease is a major BBS criterion; neurodevelopmental involvement omitted under the cap.

decisions.renal: involved: structural or functional renal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion; BBS4-specific frequency is uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: none: cognitive or developmental impairment can qualify in Bardet-Biedl syndrome, but is omitted under the cap; subtype-specific frequency is uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: postaxial polydactyly is a cardinal diagnostic feature of the Bardet-Biedl phenotype represented by this concept's child.

basis: Mandibulofacial dysostosis, ear abnormalities and lower eyelid coloboma define the phenotype. Cleft palate occurs in 1/2 annotated patients, supporting gastrointestinal involvement.

decisions.ocular: primary: lower eyelid coloboma is a characteristic diagnostic malformation of Treacher Collins syndrome, present in 2/3 annotated patients.
